comments.author: @leechumbley5440
comments.text: I had no idea that it was in Macau that Matteo Ricci and Adam Schall von Bell learnt Chinese in the highest registers of the language. I thought they landed in Peking and the rest was 'learning by doing.' Ironic that it was Portugal that wanted to get rid of all its overseas including Macao and the Chinese were not especially interested in getting involved.  Love the black spoonbills. Very interesting video.

replies.author: @leechumbley5440
replies.text: @WhereonEarth4K Casinos hold no interest for me. The history of Macau was fascinating, beginning right with the Portugese bowdlerized misunderstaning of the Ming temple of Amma Gau and continuing with St. Paul’s College, the Japanese Christian exiles and the remarkable Jesuit Sinologists. I presumed Macau had had a formal written treaty with the Middle Kingdom, but it seems life and governance had simply carried on according to “We’ve always done it that way.“ Interesting that the casino is on 100% reclaimed land.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: Thank you for such a thoughtful read, and the spoonbills are a favourite of ours too. Did the film change how you picture Macau, or had you already seen that side of it?
